name: Topology: R^3 is simply connected and a wormhole spatial section is not; no continuous metric deformation on a fixed manifold changes topology

source.located: No single source: the tree cites none (create.py:24-26, phase1.py:50-52 state it uncited). The mathematical content is standard algebraic topology (pi_1(R^3)=1; pi_1(S^1xS^2)=Z; a metric family on a fixed manifold leaves the manifold fixed), re-derived here. Its use for WORMHOLES is read in: (a) Hochberg & Visser, 'Geometric structure of the generic static traversable wormhole throat', arXiv:gr-qc/9704082v1 (1997), abstract and sec. 1; (b) Pisana, Shoshany, Antoniou, Kauffman, Lambropoulou, 'Wormhole Nucleation via Topological Surgery in Lorentzian Geometry', arXiv:2505.02210v4 (the paper create.py:125 itself cites), sec. I.A, II (0-surgery list), III.A (Def. 6, Thm III.1-III.2), III.D; (c) Borde, arXiv:gr-qc/9406053v1, sec. IX.C (degenerate metrics).

published_statement: There is no published statement of the tree's sentence as such. What the sources READ state: 2505.02210 sec. II: '3-dimensional 0-surgery: An embedding of S^0 x D^3 is replaced by D^1 x S^2 ... This surgery corresponds to the creation of a wormhole'; sec. I.A: 'wormholes: handles attached to spacetime'; sec. I.A (Geroch as restated): 'if the two 3-manifolds are non-homeomorphic, Geroch's second theorem requires that the spacetime contains either singularities or closed timelike curves'; sec. III.D: 'all the "topological charge" is confined within a compact region'; Def. 6: a spacetime carries 'an everywhere non-degenerate time-orientable Lorentzian metric'. Hochberg-Visser (gr-qc/9704082) abstract: 'Traversable wormholes have traditionally been viewed as intrinsically topological entities in some multiply connected spacetime. Here, we show that topology is too limited a tool to accurately characterize a generic traversable wormhole: in general one needs geometric information to detect the presence of a wormhole, or more precisely to locate the wormhole throat ... we shall define the wormhole throat in terms of a 2-dimensional constant-time hypersurface of minimal area'; sec. 1: 'the Morris-Thorne class of inter-universe traversable wormholes ... requiring both exact spherical symmetry and the existence of two asymptotically flat regions'; 'many other classes of geometries that one might still quite reasonably want to classify as wormholes, that ... have trivial topology'; 'A simple example of a wormhole with trivial topology is a single closed Friedman-Robertson-Walker spacetime connected by a narrow neck to ordinary Minkowski space'. Borde IX.C: 'Horowitz has shown that it is possible to construct reasonable topology-changing spacetimes if degenerate metrics are allowed.'
published_hypotheses: (math) the manifold is FIXED across the family and each g_s is a nondegenerate metric on it for every s in the CLOSED interval [0,1] -- then topology is unchanged by definition
(math) 'wormhole' = a manifold carrying a 1-handle: R^3 # (S^1 x S^2), the result of 3-dimensional 0-surgery (2505.02210 sec. II); pi_1 = Z

(Hochberg-Visser) a wormhole is defined GEOMETRICALLY by a throat: a constant-time 2-surface of minimal area (zero mean curvature) with flare-out; under this definition wormholes with TRIVIAL topology exist, and the Morris-Thorne inter-universe class has two asymptotically flat ends

(2505.02210 / Geroch as restated) topology change between non-homeomorphic slices needs a non-product cobordism, hence CTCs or singularities for a nondegenerate time-orientable Lorentzian metric; the change can be confined to a compact region
(Borde IX.C) allowing degenerate metrics at isolated points admits topology-changing spacetimes -- outside 'nondegenerate g_s on a fixed manifold'
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED -- the handle (intra-universe, non-simply-connected) restriction on 'wormhole'. create.py:24 'R^3 IS SIMPLY CONNECTED AND A WORMHOLE IS NOT', create.py:153 docstring, create.py:325-326 verdict and phase1.py:50-51 say it of 'a wormhole' unqualified. Counterexamples computed here: the Morris-Thorne inter-universe section R x S^2 IS simply connected (C3: edge-path group of S^2 trivial), and a Hochberg-Visser trivial-topology wormhole has section R^3 itself. The restriction is KEPT where it bears load: specthm.py:63 'W the throat gate (non-simply-connected topology)' and specthm.py:731 'A shortcut through non-simply-connected spatial topology'. For R x S^2 the tree's conclusion still survives but through a different invariant (H_2 = Z, two ends), not simple connectivity.

WIDENED -- 'throat' substituted for 'handle'. phase1.py:57-58 'CREATING a throat is a TOPOLOGY problem with its own theorem', create.py:41-42 'CREATE bring a throat into existence where there was none. A TOPOLOGY problem', and the canonical merged name 'a metric deformation on a fixed manifold cannot produce a throat'. Under Hochberg-Visser's geometric throat definition this is false: C4 exhibits a smooth, compactly supported family g_s = dr^2 + R_s(r)^2 dOmega^2 on FIXED R^3 (g_s = g_0 outside 1<r<3) which acquires a minimal 2-sphere with flare-out (R'=0, R''=14.2>0 at r=1.993) from s* ~ 0.277 on. What needs topology change is a HANDLE (or a second end), not a throat. The throat so made opens into a bounded 'bag', not a shortcut, so it is not a gate in create.py's sense.

MIS-ATTRIBUTED (internal discrepancy, not a refutation) -- create.py:15-16 assigns 'ON A FIXED MANIFOLD' to D1; phase1.py:16-17 puts it in the definition's preamble; create.py:18-19 table and create.py:138 hard-code D1 YES, D2 NO. C5 computes that the handle's topology change is confined to a ball (R^3 # (S^1xS^2) is R^3 with one ball replaced; the boundary of the removed ball is one 2-sphere), which is also 2505.02210 sec. III.D's 'confined within a compact region'. So compact support (D2's 'g_s = g_0 outside K') is not what the handle violates; the fixed-manifold clause is. The conclusion 'the gate is not a phase1 transition' is unaffected; which condition fails is recorded as a discrepancy.

IMPLICIT, NOW NAMED -- nondegeneracy of g_s at every s in the closed [0,1]. create.py:24-26 'at ANY support' is exact only under it; Borde IX.C (Horowitz) and 2505.02210 sec. I.A (metric degeneracies, Morse singularities) are the escapes outside it. The tree does not use those escapes and does not claim to exclude them.

HARD-CODED -- create.py:152-155 fails_on_topology() returns the literal True; create.py:271's chk compares the literal to True. The check is a restatement, not a computation; this audit's C2/C5 supply the computation for the handle class.

The only empirical premise is the hypothesis 'the background is R^3 spatially' (create.py hypotheses); C6 shows the handle conclusion does not depend on it: H_1(T^3 # S^1xS^2) = Z^4 != Z^3 = H_1(T^3), so adding a handle changes ANY closed background, simply connected or not.

later_literature.what: Wormholes defined geometrically by a minimal-area throat with flare-out; explicitly include wormholes with trivial topology and inter-universe (two-end) Morris-Thorne wormholes. So 'a wormhole is not simply connected' holds only for the intra-universe handle class, and 'creating a throat' is not in general a topology change (computed in C4).

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result: nothing in the core claim depends on data. pi_1(R^3)=1 and pi_1(R^3#(S^1xS^2))=Z are theorems of topology, computed here exactly (C1, C2), and 'no metric family on a fixed manifold changes its topology' is true by definition given nondegeneracy; no datum any author lacked could move them. The one empirical premise, 'the background is spatially R^3', is not measured at cosmological scale (global cosmic topology constraints, e.g. Planck matched-circle searches, NAMED-NOT-READ here), but C6 shows the handle conclusion is independent of it: a handle raises rank H_1 by one on T^3 as on S^3. What moved is not data but DEFINITION: after 1988 the literature (Hochberg-Visser 1997, READ) separated the geometric throat from the topological handle and exhibited simply connected and trivial-topology wormholes. Against that later definition the tree's unqualified 'a wormhole is not simply connected' and 'creating a throat is a topology problem' are too wide (C3, C4). Evidence the other way: for the object the tree actually builds on -- specthm W, 'a shortcut through non-simply-connected spatial topology' (specthm.py:731) -- the claim holds exactly, and the downstream use ('W is not a phase1 transition') is untouched.
grade_evidence: The claim STANDS for the class the tree's load-bearing site names: a non-simply-connected (handle, intra-universe) spatial section cannot arise from R^3 by any nondegenerate metric family on the fixed manifold, at any support (C1/C2/C5/C6 computed; 2505.02210 read). It is NARROWER than the sentence as written at create.py:24, 153, 325-326 and phase1.py:50-51 ('a wormhole is not'), and than its extension to throats at phase1.py:57-58 / create.py:41-42: (i) the Morris-Thorne inter-universe section R x S^2 is simply connected (C3; the conclusion survives there only via H_2 / two ends); (ii) a geometric throat in Hochberg-Visser's sense is produced by a compactly supported metric family on fixed R^3 (C4). Also recorded, not a refutation: the handle is compact-support topology (C5), so the condition it violates is the fixed-manifold clause (create.py:15 calls it D1) rather than D2 as hard-coded at create.py:138. Not WRONG: no counterexample touches the operative class; not DATA-DEPENDENT: no datum enters.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: create.py:24/153/325 and phase1.py:50-51 restricted to 'an intra-universe (handle) wormhole', 'throat' at phase1.py:57-58 and create.py:41-42 replaced by 'handle / second end', and the failing condition named as the fixed-manifold clause -- the mathematics would then match its hypotheses exactly. To WRONG: a nondegenerate metric family on a fixed manifold diffeomorphic to R^3 whose endpoint has nontrivial pi_1 -- impossible by C1 (the manifold, hence pi_1, is fixed). Reading Visser 1995 pp. 53-74, 89-93 (NAMED-NOT-READ) could sharpen which wormhole taxonomy the tree should cite but cannot move the grade.
